caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 53 of 2011 with Civil Rule No. 652 (FM) of 2010.
lawyer:
Monsur Habib, Advocate—For Appellants 
Md Kazi Akhter Hossain, Advocate—For the Respondent No.1
parties:
Sonali Food Products (Pvt) Ltd. And others ----- Appellant
 Vs
Premier Bank Ltd. And others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Anwarul Haque J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the opposite-part No. 1-4-appellants against the Order No. 11 dated 1-11-2010 and Order No. 12 dated 14-11-2010 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 47 of 2010 rejecting the application filed on behalf of the judgment-debtor nos. 1 and 2 under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, for short the Ain, for setting aside the auction sale and to refuse to execute the decree. 

 2. The facts necessary for disposal of this Appeal, in short, are that the respondent No. 1, the Premier Bank Ltd., Khatunganj Branch, Chittagong, represented by its Manager as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 96 of 2005 on 28-8-2005 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong against the present appellants and others as defendants for realization of loan money. The suit was ultimately decreed on 3-8-2009 and pursuant thereto the decree-holder put the decree into execution in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 85 of 2008 which was disposed of on 4-8-2009 on compromise that the judgment-debtors would make full payment of the loan amount to the decree-holder within 3-11-2009. The land as described in schedule-B to the decree was amicably sold out and the sale proceeds was adjusted with the decretal amount. As per said compromise the judgment-debtors were required to adjust the balance decretal amount within 3-11-2009, but they defaulted. So, the decree-holder filed the instant Artha Rin Execution Case No. 47 of 2010 in the same Adalat for sale of the schedule land except the land already sold out. Thereafter, in the process of the execution case auction notice was published in the newspaper on 2-10-2010 fixing on 27-10-2010 for sale. The Executing Court on 27-10-2010 opened the tender box and accepted the tender of the highest bidder fixing on 1-11-2010 for further Order. That on 1-11-2010 the judgment-debtor nos. 1 and 2 filed an application in the Executing Court under Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Ain for setting aside the auction sale and to refuse to execute the decree as being time barred. The learned Judge of the Executing Court vide his impugned Order No. 11 dated 1-11-2010 rejected the said application and vide another impugned Order No. 12 dated 14-11-201 confirmed the said auction sale. 

 4. The decree-holder-petitioner as respondent No. 1 entered appearance by filing power in this Appeal and filed an application for dismissing the Appeal on the ground of maintainability contending, inter alia, that as per provision of section 41 of the Ain, the appellants have not deposited 50% of the decretal amount either with the decree-holder-respondent No. 1 in the Court concerned before filing of the instant Appeal. It is also contended that depositing of 50% of the decretal amount is a condition precedent for filing of an Appeal and the appellate Court shall not admit any Appeal for hearing if such deposit is not made and a receipt of such deposit is not Annexed with the petition of Appeal and, as such, the instant Appeal is liable to be dismissed as not maintainable in law. 

 5. Mr Md Kazi Akhter Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the decree-holder-respondent No. 1 placing before us the instant petition of Appeal and the application filed on behalf the respondent No. 1 for dismissing the Appeal on the ground of maintain-ability, contends that the instant Appeal is not maintainable as the appellants have not deposited 50% of the decretal amount with the decree-holder-Bank nor in the Court concerned and, as such, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed. In support of his contention Mr. Hossain refers to the decision reported in 59 DLR (AD) 226. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the petition of Appeal, the application filed on behalf of the respondent No. 1, the impugned Orders and other materials on record. Since maintainability of the instant miscellaneous Appeal has been assailed by the decree-holder-respondent No. 1, the said issue needs to be dealt with. In this regard, let us have a look at the relevant provisions of the Ain. 

 12. On a perusal of the aforesaid provision of section 41 of the Ain it appears that any party in Order to prefer an Appeal before this Court against any Order or decree of the Artha Rin Adalat is required to file the said Appeal within 60 days and deposit 50% of the decretal amount and submit with the memorandum of Appeal the proof of such deposit and it has further been provided that in the absence of submitting such proof with memorandum of Appeal no Appeal filed under sub-section (1) of section 41 of the Ain shall be accepted for any action. In sub-section (1) of section 41 of the Ain the period for filing an Appeal has been mentioned and it has also been mentioned that such Appeal is to be filed subject to sub-section (2) of section 41 of the Ain prescribing, as we have already noticed, the requirement of submission of proof of deposit of 50% of the decretal amount. If the provision of sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) of section 41 of the Ain are read meticulously it shall be crystal clear that filing of Appeal under sub-section (1) is subject of fulfillment of the requirement of sub-section (2) of section 41 of the Ain and both the provisions are, therefore, conjunctive and not disjunctive at all. 

 "At the time of tendering the Memorandum of Appeal before the High Court Division the appellant did not deposit half of the decretal amount in the trial Court. Nowhere in section 7 it is provided that such deposit beyond the period of 30 days from the decree in compliance with the requirement of section 7 for the purpose of entertainment of a Memorandum of Appeal. Even, on the event of granting time by the High Court Division for depositing the same as contended by the learned Advocate of the petitioner, the deposit in the instant case not having been made within the statutory time cannot be construed to be a valid deposit for entertainment of a Memorandum of Appeal." 

 15. In the instant case there is no denial that as per provision of section 41 of the Ain the present appellants have not deposited 50% of the decretal amount either with the decrees holder-respondent No. 1 nor in the Court concerned before filing of the instant Appeal nor even at any subsequent date.
